newsitem.title: UK: Rugby union-Australia already plotting next year's campaign.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union-Australia already plotting next year's campaign.

text.p: Australia are already plotting next year's campaign against New Zealand after completing a clean sweep of test victories in Italy, Scotland, Ireland and Wales.

A 28-19 win over Wales on Sunday was largely overshadowed by David Campese's farewell to test rugby, but coach Greg Smith believes he has the basis of a team to worry the All Blacks in the next Tri-Nations series.
"I think we're a lot closer to them than people would imagine," said Smith. "They're the best team in the world but we're catching them. We've got some fantastic talent."
Wallaby supporters had to concede, however, their side showed little of the flamboyance shown by the impressive New Zealand Barbarians at Twickenham 24 hours earlier.

Even without three established locks, including captain John Eales, the Wallabies should have won by a wider margin but the displays of their unbeaten midweek side suggests Super 12 rugby has increased the strength in depth in Australia.
Wales, who welcomed back three former rugby league internationals, are meanwhile still searching for a consistent blend and have now lost their last six encounters with Australia.
Fly-half Jonathan Davies converted five out of five attempts at goal in his first union test for eight years but was unable to spark the Welsh side into prolonged life.

He is likely to be named again in the Welsh side to face South Africa on December 15, although romantic notions of a place on next year's Lions tour to the Republic have already been exposed to the chill winds of reality.
"I thoroughly enjoyed it, although I was a bit apprehensive before the start," said Davies. "I won't be in awe of it next time."
Wales are also hoping for a resolution to the contractual problems which have prevented Scott Quinnell slotting into the back-row.
